title: Deep Learning of Compositional Targets with Hierarchical Spectral Methods
claim: The target is a layered composition: a sparse low-degree latent feature map followed by a degree-2 feature map and scalar readout.
layout: Single vertical pyramid, bottom-to-top, with right-hand labels and formulas aligned to each layer
description: A vertical stack of white rectangular boxes joined by thick black arrows, read from bottom to top. The bottom box is the data x in R^d with a Gaussian distribution. The next box up holds the degree-k Hermite features H_k(x). A wide grey trapezoid narrows from there to the box for the latent vector h^(1) in R^{d^epsilon}, with Gaussian weights A^(1). Above that sit the degree-2 features H_2(h^(1)). A grey triangle narrows to the scalar h^(2), which is mapped by g* to the label y. On the right, pink banners in red text name each space: Space of data, Space of degree-k features, Space of degree-2 features of h^(1), and Label. Formulas for the sparse selection d_1 = d^epsilon and for the definitions of h^(1) and h^(2) sit beside the layers. The eye goes first to the grey funnels.
caption: The compositional target functions defined in Section [ref].
abstract: Why depth yields a computational advantage over shallow methods remains a central open question in learning theory. We study this question in a controlled high-dimensional Gaussian setting, focusing on compositional target functions. We analyze their learnability using an explicit three-layer fitting model trained via layer-wise spectral estimators. The target combines polynomial latent features with a scalar readout, and its compositional structure allows learning to proceed in stages. Recovering an intermediate representation reduces the problem to lower-degree spectral estimation tasks, as in multi-index models. Our analysis establishes Gaussian comparison bounds for projected moments when $0<\varepsilon<1/3$, and motivates separations in sample complexity between two- and three-layer learning strategies, conditional on a conjectured spectral recovery step.
